messages.subject: Store results of different users?
parts:
Dear all, 

so far I've just played around with shiny and rather used it as an interface that helps non-R users to get access to R graphics and data in the sense of interactively looking at an analysis. 
Now I wonder how I could set up something that rather gathers data, like in an online survey or exam? Assume I would like to use simple jquery to track some mouse clicks, like here: http://www.electrictoolbox.com/jquery-mouse-co-ordinates/
and store them to an R object. I want to store a separate R object for every visitor. So every time a user visits the site a new object should be created and once the user clicks 'save' all coordinates should be stored. 
Is there a way to do just that? Or is shiny rather intended to browse existing data an analysis?

thanks for any feedback in advance

matt

messages.subject: Re: Store results of different users?
parts:
You can store a separate R object for every visitor, by declaring that object within 

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  # here!
})

The server function is executed once at the beginning of each page load, so any local variables in that scope belong to you alone.

If you want your outputs to change when the R object changes, then you want to use reactiveValues:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  userValues <- reactiveValues()
  userValues$clicks <- c()

  observe(function() {
    # make_dataframe_from_input is just a stand-in for however you turn your jquery
    # input into the dataframe or whatever that you need
    userValues$clicks <- make_dataframe_from_input(input$clicks)
  })

  output$table <- reactiveTable({
    userValues$clicks
  })
})

To actually collect the mouse clicks you'll need to write an input binding, there's a tutorial section for that.
